about.title: Lomita Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Lomita is a small, close-knit community of about 20,785 people, and when a traffic death occurs here, it touches the whole city. Public crash records show 29 injury collisions and 36 injuries in the most recent reporting year, with one traffic death, and Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to see the most activity — often along Pacific Coast Highway, Western Avenue, Lomita Boulevard, or Palos Verdes Drive North. If you've lost a spouse, parent, or child in a crash on one of these corridors or elsewhere in the city, California law gives certain family members the right to pursue a wrongful death claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free connection service that puts grieving families in touch with an independent personal injury attorney who handles these cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is made. You focus on your family; let someone else look at the legal side.

whyChoose.title: Why Lomita Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Can Be Confusing
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then other dependents or heirs. An attorney can quickly tell you where you fit and how to proceed.

items.title: The Clock Starts at the Date of Death
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity have a much shorter window. Getting matched with an attorney early helps protect that deadline.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral costs and lost financial support, but also for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance — losses that are real but harder to put a number on. An attorney can help make sure nothing is overlooked.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs under California law may be able to bring the claim. An attorney can review your family's situation and confirm who has standing.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Lomita?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If the crash involved a government vehicle or a dangerous condition on public property, such as certain intersections along Lomita Boulevard or Palos Verdes Drive North, the deadline can be much shorter, so it helps to act sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as the criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they're separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action a family pursues to recover their own losses. One can move forward regardless of what happens in the other.

items.question: What does LawProactive actually do?
items.answer: We're not a law firm — we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who takes wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money for your family. There's no cost or obligation to simply ask questions and learn where you stand.
